summary: Clearwater County, ID tower: a 1923 log cabin, a 1931 60-foot pole tower, a 1934 50-foot L-4 tower, destroyed in 1963; the site is now reportedly a gravel pit.

facts.design: 50-foot pole L-4 tower (1934), after a 60-foot pole tower with enclosed platform (1931)
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1963 per two listings; Forest Lookouts gives no destruction date; Idaho Fire Lookouts says a gravel pit covers the likely tower site
facts.agency: Clearwater Timber Protective Association (Forest Lookouts); Clearwater National Forest (Idaho Fire Lookouts)

visit.trail_note: Labeled Drive-up by Idaho Fire Lookouts; the tower is gone and no source says whether the site is open now

events.note: Road from headquarters to the lookout reported completed, by way of Dull Axe lookout, with about two miles of spur road to Dull Axe still to build (Lewiston Morning Tribune, January 25, 1939, as quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Destroyed; neither listing gives a cause

evidence.supports: 1923 log cabin; 1931 60-foot pole tower with enclosed platform; 1934 50-foot pole L-4 tower; destroyed 1963
evidence.quote: 1923: log cabin. 1931: 60' pole tower with enclosed platform. 1934: 50' pole L-4 tower. Destroyed 1963.

evidence.supports: road completed from headquarters to the lookout, January 1939
evidence.quote: Completed the construction of road leading from Headquarters to Browns Rock lookout by way of Dull Axe lookout.

evidence.supports: report attributed to the Lewiston Morning Tribune
about two miles of spur road to Dull Axe still to build
evidence.quote: There still remains about two miles of spur road to build from this road to Dull Axe lookout.

evidence.supports: logging and gravel pit appear to have removed the site from the map
evidence.quote: Logging and a gravel pit appear to have almost completely removed the site of Browns Rock LO from the map.

evidence.supports: highest point, most likely tower site, now a gravel pit
evidence.quote: The highest point where the tower most likely was located is now the site of a gravel pit

evidence.supports: agency given as Clearwater National Forest
agency given as Clearwater Timber Protective Association
listed under the Clearwater County heading

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts names the Clearwater Timber Protective Association and Idaho Fire Lookouts names the Clearwater National Forest; the story reports both without choosing one

notes_for_editor: The 1963 destruction date appears on two listings; Forest Lookouts gives no destruction date. The Clearwater National Forest lookout list PDF (fs.usda.gov) has Destroyed 1963 rows for other sites, but no Browns Rock row turned up in it, so it does not confirm the date and is not cited. Current site is described only as a gravel pit by Idaho Fire Lookouts, a hobbyist listing. The brief recorded no events, so the 1923, 1931, 1934, 1939 and 1963 events are new.
